one_liner: Rust Perl 5 interpreter with bytecode VM and Cranelift JIT; beats perl 5 on tiny scripts, LuaJIT only on three gamed rows.
what_it_does: stryke parses and runs Perl 5 source (plus its own extensions: fn, structs, enums, match, |> pipelines, pmap/pgrep parallel builtins and a very large builtin library) as a CLI (stryke, st, s) or as the Rust library crate `stryke`. It is a Perl runtime, not a Lua or general-purpose JIT, so against LuaJIT it is only a 'which scripting runtime' comparison. It is not a full perl replacement: XS modules do not run beyond a native subset of List::Util, Scalar::Util and POSIX, and docs/BUGS.md lists 181 bug and parity entries (23 marked fixed).
how_it_is_fast: Source is lowered to bytecode for a match-dispatch VM with NaN-boxed u64 values and frame-local slot ops; hot loops and linear subs go through a Cranelift block JIT, and string-bearing segments through the author's fusevm Cranelift JIT. Several benchmark rows are carried by idiom recognisers rather than the JIT: `map { $_ * K }` and `grep { $_ % M == R }` compile to the native superinstructions MapIntMul and GrepIntModEq (map_grep_fast.rs), `sort { $a <=> $b }` becomes a native Rust sort_by (sort_fast.rs), fib-shaped recursive subs run in fib_like_tail.rs, and non-/g regex matches are memoised on (pattern, flags, haystack).
when_to_use: Existing Perl 5 one-liners and short scripts where perl's interpreter overhead dominates, and you can test them against stryke's parity gaps first.
Data-parallel scripting over all cores with pmap/pgrep/pfor (rayon work stealing) when you want Perl syntax instead of Python or Go.
Integer-heavy loops and numeric sorts in Perl syntax, where the block JIT and the native sort path apply.
Interactive or shell-pipeline use (-n/-p/-e) on Linux or macOS where a 3 ms start-up is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: As a LuaJIT substitute: it runs Perl, not Lua, and LuaJIT is faster on 5 of the 8 README rows (startup, fib, string, hash 3.4x, map_grep 4.2x).
Perl code that relies on CPAN XS modules or exact perl semantics: XS is unsupported apart from a native subset, and docs/BUGS.md documents about 158 open parity gaps and bugs.
Long-running steady-state compute you want to judge from the README: every row includes process start-up and lasts 2-14 ms, and no steady-state comparison with LuaJIT is published.

Windows or minimal-footprint deployments: CI builds only x86-64 Linux and x86-64/aarch64 macOS, the README cites a 44 MB static binary, and the crate pulls a large dependency tree (Cranelift, PCRE2, ureq, svg2pdf, pdf-extract, zshrs, fusevm).
Projects needing a mature, widely used runtime: 5 stars, one author, 219 crate versions since 2026-04-19.

integration.form: crate (library `stryke`, also built as a staticlib) plus CLI binaries stryke / st / s; Homebrew tap
integration.dependencies: rayon, regex, fancy-regex, pcre2 (C PCRE2), cranelift 0.130 (jit, codegen, frontend, native, module), fusevm 0.26.7, zshrs 0.13.1, crossbeam, dashmap, ureq, svg2pdf, pdf-extract and many more (about 200 dependency lines in Cargo.toml)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust stable, edition 2021 (no rust-version field; CI uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable)
integration.platforms: x86-64 Linux, x86-64 and aarch64 macOS (CI release matrix); Windows not built in CI; signal-hook is a unix-only dependency
integration.thread_safety: Each parallel block runs an isolated VM with a captured scope on rayon workers; shared state goes through varsync (Arc<Mutex>); thread safety of the embedding API is not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — not a drop-in for LuaJIT (different language); for perl 5 it runs many scripts via `stryke script.pl` (with --compat for strict Perl semantics) but not XS modules, and documented parity gaps remain

gotchas: Harness flaw in the regex row: bench_regex.pl matches one constant string against one constant pattern 100,000 times, and regex_match_execute (interpreter.rs in 0.7.7, vm_helper.rs now) returns the memoised result whenever pattern, flags, multiline and haystack equal the previous non-/g match, so the regex engine runs once and the other 99,999 iterations are a string compare. The 0.07x vs LuaJIT (which runs Lua patterns every iteration) and 7.1x vs perl measure the memo, not regex speed. In v0.7.7, the build behind the table, the memo was keyed on the uninterpolated pattern text, so a loop over an interpolated pattern (/^$p/) on an unchanged string replayed a stale answer; the current source carries a comment describing that fix.

Other rows also hit shape-specific paths that the perturbed-source check in run_bench.sh cannot catch, because it only renames $i/$sum/$count: map_grep uses MapIntMul and GrepIntModEq superinstructions, array uses a native Rust sort_by for { $a <=> $b } on already-sorted input (a single run, against LuaJIT's C quicksort calling the comparator), and fib uses the fib_like evaluator. All four paths are present in the published 0.7.7 crate, whose bench scripts match the current ones apart from the fib sub's name.

All rows include process start-up: stryke's startup row (3.3 ms) is above its loop row (3.2 ms), and it is slower than perl (2.3 ms) and LuaJIT (1.5 ms) on start-up, although the README text says stryke beats perl on all 8.
The README numbers come from v0.7.7 (crates.io, published 2026-04-19); the current crate is 0.17.59, and no newer table has been published.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick stryke only when the code is Perl and you want a faster perl; for a fast embeddable scripting JIT, LuaJIT itself, WrenJIT or libriscv have like-for-like LuaJIT comparisons, and XS (xs-lang) has the same start-up-dominated timing caveat.
verified_claims_summary: README table from bench/run_bench_all.sh (hyperfine, mean of 10 runs after 3 warmups, process start-up included) on an Apple M5 with 18 cores: stryke v0.7.7 beats LuaJIT 2.1.1774896198 on loop (3.2 vs 4.3 ms), array (9.8 vs 59.0 ms) and regex (12.6 vs 178.2 ms), and loses the other five rows. Against perl 5.42.2 it wins 7 of 8 rows, losing start-up. The regex win comes from a match-result memo, the array win from a native sort of presorted input, and fib from a fib-shape evaluator.
status_note: Very active single-author MIT project (1,983 commits, last commit 2026-10-05, 0.17.59 on crates.io, 5 stars) and installable via cargo or Homebrew. Its benchmark evidence is a stale v0.7.7 table whose regex, array, map_grep and fib rows are carried by memoisation and idiom fast paths, so treat the LuaJIT claim as unproven.
